Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks again for the call today  great alignment. I wanted to recap the key success criteria and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC plan. Please review and confirm or call out anything missing.

Success criteria (what ACME will evaluate)
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for 1k token inference, 95% of calls during peak window
- Cost: target unit cost <= $0.002 per generated token (goal, used for comparison)
- Quality: >= 85% pass rate on the bench of 3,000 representative prompts (we'll run A/B vs current model)
- Reliability: 99.9% uptime during the 2-week POC window

Evaluation plan
- You will provide the prompt set and expected outputs (we can host evaluation rigs on the shared Drive).
- We'll run automated scoring and provide per-prompt diffs + examples for failed cases.
- Weekly checkpoints (end of week 1 & week 2) for findings and tuning.

Proposed timeline
- Technical deep-dive (60m): week of Jun 29 (your availability?)
- POC setup and integration: Jul 6 - Jul 17 (2 weeks)
- Final results and recommendation: Jul 20

Owners
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (POC lead), Dev Patel (integration engineer), Vivek Kulkarni (runtime/ops)
- ACME: Alex Johnson (product), Priya Menon (security/compliance)

Next steps
1) Confirm success criteria above and your availability for the 60m technical deep-dive.
2) We will share an integration checklist and sample SDK snippets prior to the deep-dive (attached: ACME_POC_scope.pdf).
3) Confirm if you need VPC/private deployment details during the POC.

Attachments: ACME_POC_scope.pdf

Thanks  talk soon.

Perfect  thanks Alex. Adding Dev + Vivek to scope the integration details and surface any content/security considerations.

High-level integration plan (we'll expand in the deep-dive and share a runnable checklist):
- Auth: API key for dev POC; for private deployments we support token + KMS-backed keys.
- SDKs: Node and Python SDKs available; we'll provide sample snippets and a small reference app.
- API surface: standard REST endpoints (/v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings) + streaming via SSE/websocket for low-latency token-by-token delivery.
- Tool calling: function-calling available (JSON schema-based)  model responses can return structured tool call objects; runtime will emit events to the tracing pipeline for every tool invocation.
- Data routing: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: we can run the POC on hosted with optional VPC peering if you need private network paths.
- Fallbacks: we recommend a canary config: primary model + a smaller fallback for overload; we can configure automatic fallback on latency thresholds.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (will upload), ACME_POC_scope.pdf

Dev / Vivek  can you prepare a short integration doc for the deep-dive showing: SDK quickstart, example API routes, streaming example, and a simple tool-calling JSON schema example?

Marissa

Subject: Redwood integration plan (SDK, API routes, streaming, tool calling)

Hi all  below is a concise technical plan / checklist I'll present during the deep-dive. Happy to add more detail if useful.

1) Quickstart (Node)
- npm install @redwood/inference
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=your_key_here
- const {Client} = require('@redwood/inference');
- const client = new Client();
- const resp = await client.generate({model: 'redwood-1-large', input: 'Summarize this...'});

2) REST endpoints (examples)
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>, Content-Type: application/json
  Body: {"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":512}

- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
  (chat messages array, role-based)

3) Streaming (SSE / websocket)
- Streaming endpoint: GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream?model=redwood-1-large
- Server-sent events push partial tokens with event types: token, done, error
- Example: we send token deltas every 20-50ms for low-latency UX; client can buffer or render incrementally.

4) Tool calling / function calling
- The model may respond with a special JSON blob: {"tool_call": {"name":"lookup_customer","args":{...}}}
- Redwood runtime will emit tracing events for each tool request and response; by default events are pushed to our tracing console and can be forwarded to your observability hooks.

5) Auth / security notes
- For this POC we recommend API keys + optional IP allowlist or VPC peering.
- For customer-managed keys we support KMS/HSM integrations for encryption at rest.

6) Fallbacks & canary
- Configurable routing policy: primary model -> fallback model (smaller) when latency exceeds threshold.

7) Rollout and rollback
- Canary to 5% for 24h, monitor error/latency, then scale to 50/100% with automated rollback on regression.

Example cURL (non-streaming):
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"Write a short summary of the following...","max_tokens":150}'

Notes / questions for ACME for the deep-dive:
- Do you want SSE or websocket streaming? Which client platforms (web / mobile / server) will you prioritize?
- For tool calling, please share an example of a tool schema you use internally so we can show a mapping example.
- Any constraints around egress / peering for logs/traces?

I'll bring a short demo and the checklist (redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx).
